name: Diamond Kimm
bio: Diamond Kimm was a Korean-born printer and editor of the newspaper Korean Independence, a U.S. resident since 1928 and an outspoken opponent of the U.S.-backed Syngman Rhee regime. In 1959 the Ninth Circuit affirmed an order deporting him to South Korea — where, his supporters warned, he faced death — and the Supreme Court agreed to review the case.
charges: Deportation (Walter-McCarran Act) — tied to his radical, anti-Rhee politics
convicted: Deportation order affirmed 1959; Supreme Court review granted
sentence: Under deportation order; fighting removal to South Korea

name: Michael Daniels
bio: Michael ('Mike') Daniels was a Greek-born co-editor of the left-wing Greek Tribune. In May 1959, though mentally ill, he was seized from a rest home and flown toward deportation as an alien member of the Communist Party; the removal was challenged.
charges: Deportation (Walter-McCarran Act) — as an alleged alien Communist Party member
convicted: Seized for deportation May 1959; order challenged

name: Jo Ann Santiago
bio: Jo Ann Santiago, born in Canada in 1922 and brought to the United States at age six, was the wife of a Puerto Rican Communist leader. In 1959 she faced deportation after being denied an adjustment of status because she refused to answer questions about Communism; her case was on appeal.
charges: Deportation (Walter-McCarran Act) — refusal to answer questions about Communism
convicted: Denied status adjustment; deportation proceedings on appeal

name: Walter C. Lohman Jr.
bio: Walter C. Lohman Jr. was an officer of UE Local 768 in Dayton, Ohio, convicted in 1949 of filing a false non-Communist affidavit under the Taft-Hartley Act. In December 1959 the Supreme Court refused to review his case, leaving his five-year sentence to stand.
charges: Taft-Hartley Act — filing a false non-Communist affidavit
convicted: Convicted 1949; Supreme Court refused review December 1959

name: Albert Skinner
bio: Albert Skinner was one of nine present and former leaders of the independent International Union of Mine, Mill & Smelter Workers convicted in Denver in December 1959 of conspiracy to file false non-Communist affidavits under the Taft-Hartley Act — a prosecution the union condemned as an attempt to destroy it.
charges: Conspiracy to file false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Convicted of the Taft-Hartley conspiracy charge

name: Jesse Van Camp
bio: Jesse Van Camp was one of nine leaders of the Mine, Mill & Smelter Workers Union convicted in Denver in December 1959 of conspiring to file false non-Communist affidavits under the Taft-Hartley Act, in a case the union fought as an attack on its right to exist.
charges: Conspiracy to file false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Convicted of the Taft-Hartley conspiracy charge

name: Irving Dichter
bio: Irving Dichter was one of the Mine, Mill & Smelter Workers Union leaders convicted in Denver in December 1959 of conspiracy to file false non-Communist affidavits under the Taft-Hartley Act.

name: Harold Sanderson

charges: Conspiracy to file false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Convicted of the Taft-Hartley conspiracy charge

name: James H. Durkin

sentence: Convicted of the Taft-Hartley conspiracy charge

charges: Conspiracy to file false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Convicted of the Taft-Hartley conspiracy charge

name: Alton Lawrence
bio: Alton Lawrence was an executive board member of the Mine, Mill & Smelter Workers Union from Bessemer, Alabama, one of the defendants in the 1959 Denver Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' case who entered a plea of nolo contendere to the charge of filing false non-Communist affidavits.
charges: Conspiracy to file false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Resolved by no-contest plea in the Taft-Hartley case

sentence: Resolved by no-contest plea in the Taft-Hartley case

name: Albert Pezatti
bio: Albert Pezatti, who had retired the previous spring as secretary-treasurer of the Mine, Mill & Smelter Workers Union, was one of the defendants in the 1959 Denver Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' case who entered a no-contest plea to the charge of filing false non-Communist affidavits.
